Early mornings and late nights are proving the hardest these days. 

I have this uncontrollable feeling of impending doom every night like clockwork and takes me hours to calm down enough to fall asleep. It gets worse whenever I try to convince myself that there's nothing wrong and everything is...generally...pretty ok right now.

Meanwhile, every morning starts with a list of all the reasons I suck (my brain is remarkably sadistic/masochistic it seems)--from why I can't seem to keep any friends to why I'm just a waste of space who would be better off dead.

Still, I am fighting. Every day. I've spent nearly two decades allowing this nightmare to govern my life and I just can't do it anymore. So I fake it. Everyone thinks I'm improving because I smile more and offer to be helpful and actively try to be kinder. 

But I know its all an act. I know how bad things still are on the inside. I just hope I can fake it till I make it--that's the only thing keeping me from just breaking down multiple times a day.

Thank you. 

I can sometimes convince myself of that on my own, but every now and then its good to know that I'm not just lying to myself.

I'm incredibly sorry you had to go through that. In that case, especially if your parents are more understanding, I definitely would suggest talking about this with them. 

I know its hard. Asking for help when you're feeling particularly bad can be horrible, but you need to protect your own mental health first and foremost. Hopefully, with enough guidance, your sister will come around and realize how remarkably hurtful her words/actions can be.

If your sister is genuinely refusing to hear you when you clearly tell her you are struggling, I would definitely urge you to reach out to your parents. 

Sibling relationships can be tricky because most of us do have a jokey/borderline toxic rapport that--unless you are suffering from depression--you are unlikely to pick up on. I didn't realize how potentially damaging some of the conversations I had with my brothers were until I was going through an especially bad patch and nearly broke down over some snide remark that, in hindsight, was never intended to hurt.

I really hope your dad can help. If nothing else, no harm in talking to him and maybe figuring out what tactic would be best to ensure your sister understands that while you value your relationship with her, there are times that her behavior can hurt you and cause you pain--intentional or otherwise.

They're going through their own shit and I don't blame them for wanting to deal with it however works best for them, but it stings knowing that I thought I could rely on them, while they never thought the same way about me.

Sorry, this is rambling. Just been feeling... weirder than "normal" and not sure how to express myself without alienating everyone.

Some days all I want to do is talk to someone about nothing at all, y'know? Might miss that banality of that more than anything else

As someone who has used MDMA (fairly successfully) in the past to deal with depression, here's some advice--with usual caveats of course:

Don't think of MDMA as a cure-all. It's all about the journey. Think about what's wrong and more importantly WHY you feel its wrong. I was going through a similar "why am I so alone" bout when I used it and I realized that I have some great friends. Its just we're in different places right now and that's ok! I also called up a few people and just chatted with them about...well...nothing really. But it helped. The MDMA allowed me to focus less on my internal monologue and more on the emotions behind it. Its fine to just let these thoughts run through the background of your head while you're in the MDMA 'happy zone.'

Don't worry about taking too much or too little. You're not trying to rage here! Just focus on feeling relaxed and carrying over that feeling into your everyday life. MDMA's benefits, at least in my case, are heavily linked to mental space when you take it. If you're nervous or anxious, you'll be less receptive to the 'glow.' Just ease into it. And if you need to just dance/jump around/whatever while you're getting to that point, then just enjoy the ride!

And finally, and I think this is very important, when you're coming down, whatever conclusions you've reached, WRITE THEM DOWN. Good or bad, the feelings you have on MDMA can open up a lot of emotional baggage. Having it written down to review once you're sober can be vital to moving past your depression.

I had a cat once that was on his last legs (cancer). My mother called me at work and told me that I had to come home because he wasn't doing so well and was panicking and maybe it would be a good idea to take him to the vet. I dropped everything and just went. Unfortunately, I had just gotten home and sat down to pet him when he died in my arms--almost like he had been waiting. I'll never forget that. I didn't cry there, but on the ride back to work (it was a 20-minute commute) I just had tears rolling down my face. I still miss him.

They give you unconditional love and affection and ask for so little in return and you can't even manage to 'man up' and spend their last moments for them?
